lead: A turbine's four efficiencies show where the water power goes: hydraulic losses in the runner, leakage past seals, and mechanical friction in bearings. They multiply, never add. The site fixes head and discharge, while the turbine curve fixes efficiency at that flow. Selection matches the two. A small hydro plant at a canal drop uses this when summer flow falls and the chosen turbine must still run well.
prereq: You need: work done and velocity triangles from 6.4, losses in 6.5, and specific speed from 6.7.

blocks.text: Water power entering the turbine is P<sub>w</sub> = ρgQH. Here ρ is density in kg/m³, g is 9.81 m/s², Q is discharge in m³/s and H is net head in m.

blocks.where: η<sub>h</sub> is hydraulic efficiency; u₁ and u₂ are runner speeds at inlet and outlet in m/s; V<sub>w1</sub> and V<sub>w2</sub> are whirl velocities in m/s.

blocks.text: Hydraulic efficiency measures energy transferred to the runner. Volumetric efficiency accounts for water that leaks past without doing work. Mechanical efficiency accounts for bearing and seal friction.
η<sub>v</sub> = (Q − q) / Q     η<sub>m</sub> = P<sub>s</sub> / P<sub>r</sub>
blocks.where: q is leakage in m³/s; P<sub>s</sub> is shaft power; P<sub>r</sub> is runner power.
η<sub>o</sub> is overall efficiency. Multiply the three factors; adding them gives a meaningless number above 1.

blocks.text: A main curve is drawn at fixed head: hold H, change the guide-vane opening, and record discharge and efficiency. An operating curve holds speed fixed, as a grid-connected machine does, and lets head and load vary. A Muschel curve plots efficiency against speed ratio (or unit speed) for one fixed guide-vane opening at constant head, so a family of them shows how the best operating point shifts as the opening changes. The iso-efficiency hill collects many such tests; the hill's peak is the design point.

Part-load behaviour follows from velocity triangles. A Kaplan turbine has movable runner blades and guide vanes, so it re-angles the flow into the runner as Q falls and keeps the velocity triangles close to their best shape. Pelton buckets are fixed; at low Q the jet is thin and windage and bearing losses dominate, so efficiency falls quickly. Francis sits between the two.

Select in this order. Head first: high head above about 300 m points to Pelton; medium head from about 30 m to 300 m to Francis; low head below about 30 m to Kaplan. Discharge then sets the size. Specific speed confirms the family.

blocks.where: N is speed in rpm; P is shaft power in kW; H is head in m. Low N<sub>s</sub> suits Pelton, medium Francis, high Kaplan.

blocks.text: Rotational speed must match the generator. For 50 Hz, N = 120f/P<sub>p</sub> rpm, where P<sub>p</sub> is the number of poles. A 10-pole machine runs at 600 rpm. Reaction turbines also need enough submergence to avoid cavitation; the setting is checked against the manufacturer's limit, with details in Unit 7.
A governor holds speed by moving guide vanes, or a Pelton deflector, when load changes. It should correct frequency without chasing every small fluctuation.

figure.caption: Overall efficiency against discharge ratio for three turbines; the peak of each curve is the design point. Pelton peaks sharply near design flow, Francis peaks near design flow, and Kaplan stays almost flat over a wide band.

spec.aria: Efficiency against discharge ratio for Pelton, Francis and Kaplan turbines, with the peak of each curve at design flow; Pelton peaks sharply, Francis peaks near design flow, and Kaplan is a broad flat band.

examples.question: A turbine passes Q = 5 m³/s under a net head H = 60 m. Its hydraulic efficiency is 0.92, volumetric efficiency is 0.96 and mechanical efficiency is 0.97. Take ρ = 1000 kg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s². Find the overall efficiency and the shaft power.
steps: Overall efficiency: η_o = η_h η_v η_m = 0.92 × 0.96 × 0.97 = 0.856704.
examples.answer: The overall efficiency is 0.8567 and the shaft power is 2.521 MW.
examples.check:
rho=1000
g=9.81
Q=5
H=60
eta_h=0.92
eta_v=0.96
eta_m=0.97
eta_o=eta_h*eta_v*eta_m
Pw=rho*g*Q*H
Ps=eta_o*Pw
print(round(eta_o,4))
print(round(Ps/1e6,3))

traps: Adding η_h, η_v and η_m instead of multiplying them.
Using hydraulic efficiency alone as the overall efficiency.
Reading a constant-speed operating curve as if it were a constant-head main curve.
Using the design-point efficiency when the turbine runs at part load.
Mixing watts and kilowatts, or dropping ρ and g when computing water power.

quiz.q: State the four efficiencies of a turbine and the relation between them.
quiz.a: Hydraulic η_h, volumetric η_v, mechanical η_m and overall η_o = η_h η_v η_m.

quiz.q: Why are the efficiencies multiplied rather than added?
quiz.a: Each is a fraction of the power remaining after the previous loss. Multiplication chains the fractions: 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, not 1.8.

quiz.q: A turbine passes 2 m³/s under 40 m head with overall efficiency 0.85. Find the shaft power. Use ρ = 1000 kg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s².
Explain why a Kaplan turbine keeps high efficiency at part load while a Pelton wheel does not.
quiz.a: Kaplan blades and guide vanes move to keep the velocity triangles favourable as Q falls. Pelton buckets are fixed, so a thin jet at low Q raises relative windage and bearing losses and efficiency drops.

quiz.q: A site has H = 150 m and Q = 2 m³/s. Which turbine family fits, and what else must be checked before ordering?
quiz.a: Medium head points to Francis. Check specific speed, synchronous speed, part-load efficiency and the cavitation submergence limit.
A contour plot of equal overall efficiency over a map of head, discharge or speed. Its peak is the design point.

quiz.q: Distinguish a main curve from an operating curve.
quiz.a: A main curve is measured at constant head while opening or discharge changes. An operating curve is measured at constant speed while head and load vary.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern selection uses computational fluid dynamics and digital twins to predict part-load behaviour before a runner is cast. Small hydro projects in India often pair a Kaplan runner with a permanent-magnet generator for canal drops. Search next for turbine hill diagrams, model testing under IEC standards, and governor droop settings.
